name: Ghanaian Jollof Rice
description: Jollof rice, tomato-and-pepper rice cooked until it takes on real color and depth, is fiercely championed in Ghana as the true original in West Africa's long-running jollof rivalry - the real base is a fried, reduced tomato-pepper puree, not just rice simmered in canned sauce.
steps_detailed: Blend the tomatoes, bell pepper, jalapeño, and half the onion into a smooth puree.
Brown the chicken, 6-7 minutes, then set aside.
Fry the remaining onion, add the tomato paste, cook 2 minutes, then add the puree and simmer uncovered 15-18 minutes until deeply reduced.
Stir in the rice, broth, and chicken, cover, and cook on low 20-25 minutes until tender.

name: Ghanaian Waakye
description: Waakye, rice and beans cooked together with dried millet leaves or sorghum stalks that dye it a distinctive reddish-brown, is one of Ghana's most beloved everyday dishes - the coloring leaves aren't a distinct item here, so this stays its natural color.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Cowpeas (blackeyes), immature seeds, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

ingredients.ingredient: Cowpeas (blackeyes), immature seeds, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

steps_detailed: Cook the rice and cowpeas together in the same pot with enough water to cover, 18-20 minutes, until the rice is tender.

name: Ghanaian Banku
description: Banku, fermented corn and cassava dough cooked into a smooth, stretchy paste, is a genuine Ghanaian staple, traditionally eaten by hand alongside soup or grilled fish.
steps_detailed: Mix the cornmeal and grated cassava with water into a smooth batter and let sit at room temperature 12-24 hours to ferment - real banku's sour tang comes from this fermentation, not an ingredient added directly.
Cook the fermented batter over medium heat, stirring constantly, 15-18 minutes, until thick, smooth, and stretchy.

name: Ghanaian Kenkey
description: Kenkey, fermented corn dough wrapped in corn husks or banana leaves and steamed, is a genuine Ghanaian staple with a distinctive sour tang from real fermentation.
steps_detailed: Mix the cornmeal with water into a stiff dough and let ferment at room temperature 24 hours.
Shape into balls, wrap tightly, and steam over simmering water 45-50 minutes until firm and cooked through.

name: Ghanaian Groundnut Soup
description: Groundnut soup, built on real ground peanuts, is one of Ghana's most beloved soups, traditionally served with fufu or rice.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Peanuts, all types, dry-roasted, with salt

ingredients.ingredient: Peanuts, all types, dry-roasted, with salt

steps_detailed: Brown the chicken, 6-7 minutes.
Whisk the ground peanuts with 1.5 cups water into a smooth paste.
Add the peanut paste, tomatoes, and jalapeño, and simmer 20-25 minutes until thickened.

name: Ghanaian Kelewele
description: Kelewele, spiced fried ripe plantain, is a beloved Ghanaian street food, real ground ginger being the defining flavor.
steps_detailed: Toss the plantain with the ginger and chili powder.
Fry, turning, 4-5 minutes, until deeply caramelized.

name: Ghanaian Red Red
description: Red red, black-eyed peas stewed in palm-oil-red tomato sauce and served with fried plantain, gets its name from the color of both the beans' sauce and the plantain.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Cowpeas (blackeyes), immature seeds, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

ingredients.ingredient: Cowpeas (blackeyes), immature seeds, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

steps_detailed: Simmer the cowpeas with the tomatoes 12-15 minutes.
Fry the plantain slices in the remaining oil, 3-4 minutes per side, until caramelized.
Serve the beans with the fried plantain alongside.

name: Ghanaian Fufu
description: Fufu, cassava and plantain pounded together into a smooth, stretchy dough, is one of West Africa's most iconic staple starches, traditionally eaten by tearing off pieces to scoop up soup.
steps_detailed: Boil the cassava and plantain together until completely soft, 20-25 minutes.
Pound or mash vigorously until smooth and stretchy, free of lumps.

name: Ghanaian Light Soup
description: Light soup, a thin, peppery tomato broth, is a common Ghanaian everyday soup, lighter than groundnut or palm nut soup.
steps_detailed: Simmer the chicken, tomatoes, jalapeño, and onion together in 2 cups water 25-30 minutes until the chicken is tender.

name: Ghanaian Shito
description: Shito, a fiery, dark pepper and dried fish sauce, is one of Ghana's most essential condiments, spooned onto nearly anything.
steps_detailed: Blend the jalapeño and onion into a coarse paste.
Fry the paste in the oil over medium heat, stirring often, 15-18 minutes, until deeply dark and reduced - this long fry is what gives real shito its depth.
Stir in the fish sauce off the heat.

name: Ghanaian Chichinga (Suya-Style Skewers)
description: Chichinga, spiced grilled meat skewers coated in a ground peanut rub, closely related to Nigerian suya and shared across the wider West African region.

steps_detailed: Mix the ground peanuts with the paprika and chili powder.
Coat the sliced beef in the mixture and thread onto skewers.
Grill, turning, 6-8 minutes, until charred.
